m-jacksonville|2026-10-05|5100b4b4|06d5c.title:
JTA Financial Update Presentation

Randall Barnes, JTA CFO, gave a presentation about JTA's finances. Mr. Barnes talked about a budget shortfall in FY 25, reduced sales tax revenue, increased costs for unbudgeted services (Connexion Plus) and costs for NAVI and Skyway that were higher than expected. Mr. Barnes spoke about the FY26 budget, amended in February, that addressed the expected revenue shortfall, but said the plan to cut expenses was not sufficient to address the full cost to provide services. Professor Jeff Carney, University of Florida School of Architecture and Director of the Florida Institute for Built Environment Resilience (FIBER), and Dr. Changjie Chen, Assistant Scientist, FIBER, provided a presentation on the JaxTwin program.

Professor Carney explained that a digital twin is a living digital model of a city, including its buildings, infrastructure, environmental systems, and transportation, that allows people to visualize relationships and make better decisions. He stated that the team had been working on Jacksonville’s digital twin for three years, examining the city’s growth and whether the City is prepared to handle that growth given challenges such as inadequate public transportation, traffic congestion, and flooding.

He explained that the JaxTwin platform pulls together data from a wide range of sources, including transportation, the physical environment, topography, bathymetry, sea levels, flood and storm surges, housing, and demographics. He added that the platform turns that data into a legible graphic interface.

Dr. Chen then presented an agentic artificial intelligence (AI) system developed in partnership with JTA, explaining that it has two goals: serving people without cars, impoverished people, and people with disabilities, and improving transit on-time performance. He added that the AI agent evaluates these goals and generates recommendations to improve the performance of the transit system.

Overview The Tallahassee Community Redevelopment Agency Commercial Property Improvement Program (CPIP) is a reimbursement grant that offers assistance for eligible property improvements including construction, renovation, expansion and installation of permanent improvements to commercial buildings. Improvements may be exterior, interior or a combination of interior/exterior. Grants are contingent upon the availability of funds in the Tallahassee CRA budget. Grant awards are also contingent upon a demonstrated benefit to the CRA district and compliance with the Downtown or Greater Frenchtown/Southside Redevelopment Plan. Additional eligibility requirements and program features are described below.

m-tallahassee|2026-10-06|fff13807|484803.title: The Tallahassee Trust for Historic Preservation (TTHP) found that the Collins House met the criteria for listing on the Local Register of Historic Places (Sec. 10-318 (d) of the LDC). The Collins House is recognized as historically significant due to its contribution to the National Register District, retaining its significant historical architectural character, and its association with Governor LeRoy Collins as his childhood home. The ARB voted unanimously to recommend that the Collins House be placed on the Local Register of Historic Places and be rezoned to include a HPO.

m-titusville|2026-10-13|09ca3685|c5ba716.title: E. Funding Transfer for Fire Prevention Services Outsourcing Transition Approve the requested budget transfer from Fire Department Salaries and Benefits to Professional Services to support the transition of in-house fire prevention services to an outside professional service. The transition eliminates four full-time equivalent (FTE) positions, representing approximately $369,427 in annual salary and benefit expenditures. Transferring these savings to Professional Services allows the Department to fund a portion of the contracted prevention services while reducing long-term personnel costs and maintaining continuity of service. This approach provides greater operational flexibility, reduces administrative and staffing burdens, and allows the Department to align resources with current service delivery needs.
